title: Check yourself: Freshness after a re-index, measuring retrieval alone and the practice

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team reports a retrieval recall of nine in ten. It counts only the 30 labelled questions that returned something, and 27 of those had the relevant chunk in the top results. Ten more labelled questions came back empty. Which figure follows the page?

options.text: 90 percent, since only questions that returned something can be judged
options.says: Ruled out because "A question with no results counts as a miss in recall over the labelled set".

options.text: 68 percent, since a blank query still belongs in the denominator
options.says: The page says "the denominator is every labelled question", so 27 of 40 is about 68 percent.

options.text: 100 percent, since every result that was returned held the relevant chunk
options.says: Ruled out because only 27 of the 30 returned results held the relevant chunk, and "the denominator is every labelled question" in any case.

options.text: 75 percent, since 30 of the 40 labelled questions were answered
options.says: Ruled out because "and so does a question that was never answered": answered questions are not the denominator.

questions.stem: In a test of 8 questions, the evidence was retrieved for 5 and the answers were right for 5. One answer was wrong although its evidence was retrieved, and one was right although its evidence was not. How many of the questions have no retrieved evidence and a wrong answer?

options.says: Ruled out because five is the number of questions whose evidence was retrieved ("the evidence was retrieved for 5"), the opposite count.
Ruled out because the wrong answer that had its evidence is one where "The evidence was retrieved and the answer is wrong", a generation failure.
Ruled out because the right answer without evidence is one where "The answer is right although the evidence was not retrieved", a defect but not a retrieval failure by definition.
The outcomes are 4 ok, 1 generation, 2 retrieval and 1 unsupported, so two questions had no evidence and a wrong answer.
